Subject: MAP draft & next steps: Load/perf test scheduling (Acme)

Hi Samantha,

Great to speak earlier — thanks for walking us through Acme's planned rollout. Per our call, attaching a first-pass MAP (MAP_v1_ACME.docx) and a short proposed load test plan (proposed_load_test_plan.pdf).

Quick recap / asks so we can lock the load/perf milestone: 
- Goal: validate peak QPS and latency at expected production traffic so we can size Dedicated capacity and confirm SLOs.
- Redwood deliverable: run traffic replay against a dedicated capacity pool, produce sizing recommendation (nodes / GPU type), and regression report.
- Acme deliverable: provide traffic replay artifacts (sample traffic, manifests), confirm peak QPS and target test window.
- Target close date for this MAP: 2026-07-15 (aim to complete perf/signoff by end of June; final procurement in early July).

Proposed MAP milestone for load/perf test (we can edit in the doc):
1) Traffic replay delivery from Acme (manifest + sample files) — owner: Acme Infra — due: 2026-06-22
2) Redwood provisions dedicated capacity for replay (staging) — owner: Redwood infra (Marissa / Vivek) — due: 2026-06-24
3) Execute traffic replay & load tests (peak and soak) — owner: Redwood SRE (Dev) — window: 2026-06-25 to 2026-06-26
4) Analysis, sizing recommendation, and report — owner: Redwood (Marissa & Dev) — due: 2026-06-30

Questions for you to confirm:
- Can Acme deliver a traffic replay manifest (JSONL) and a sample of 1 hour of traffic by 6/22? If not, what earliest date works?
- What is the expected peak QPS we should target for the replay? Also, typical sequence length / prompt sizes you expect during peak?
- Any RATELIMITS or tokenization differences we should be aware of?

Cc'ing Marissa and Dev for capacity notes and to confirm internal owners.

Thanks — Vivek
--
Vivek Kulkarni

Subject: Re: MAP draft & next steps: Load/perf test scheduling (Acme)

Thanks Vivek — appreciate the clear MAP draft. Quick answers from our side: 

- We can deliver the traffic replay manifest and a 1-hour sample by EOD Monday 2026-06-22. We'll upload to a pre-signed S3 link and share.
- Peak QPS to target: 650 QPS sustained (95th pct burst to 900 QPS). Typical prompt/token profile: median prompt ~ 120 tokens, 95th ~ 480 tokens.
- No custom tokenization; we use standard UTF-8 text inputs. We do have some attachments in messages that lead to longer prompt sequences (we'll flag those in the manifest).

Attachments: acme_peak_qps_report.csv, traffic_replay_manifest.jsonl (sample manifest stub).

We'll confirm the exact S3 URL in a follow-up from Jorge (cc'd) who owns infra. Thanks — Samantha

Acme Corp
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-19T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft & next steps: Load/perf test scheduling (Acme)

Thanks Sam/Vivek — technical notes and a couple of asks from the Redwood SRE side: 

1) For sizing: given the 650 QPS sustained / 900 QPS burst and median token lengths you provided, initial estimate is to provision a dedicated pool equivalent to ~6-8 A100-class GPUs (in our benchmarking environment) with continuous batching enabled. Exact node/GPU mix will depend on batch size and KV cache behavior.

2) Replay artifacts: we need the manifest to include per-request metadata (timestamp, user-id hash, sequence length, and any pinned stop tokens). The sample we saw looks good but please include a small subset of long sequences (>=400 tokens) so we can validate memory and KV cache effects.

3) Concurrency: one important input is the number of concurrent request streams vs QPS (e.g., 650 QPS could be 650 single-stream requests or 65 streams of 10 RPS). If you can annotate concurrency model in the manifest that helps us pick batching and worker configs.

4) Timezones: to minimize customer impact we'll run the replay in your staging environment. Proposed test windows (please confirm):
   - PST window: 2026-06-25 02:00 - 08:00 (off-peak for Acme prod)
   - Alternative: 2026-06-26 22:00 - 04:00 PST

5) Data handling & logs: Redwood will keep replay logs for 30 days by default; if you need longer retention let us know.

I'll plan to start cluster provisioning once we have the S3 link and manifest.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
